title: repo-server stops reading `ARGOCD_REPO_OTLP_HEADERS` — rename it to `ARGOCD_REPO_SERVER_OTLP_HEADERS`

detection.reason: checked on the repo-server Deployment's container env NAMES only — the default manifests set the new name, so the old one is present only when a patch or Helm values added it by hand

quote: If you set `ARGOCD_REPO_OTLP_HEADERS` directly (for example via a custom Deployment patch or Helm values), rename it to `ARGOCD_REPO_SERVER_OTLP_HEADERS`. The old variable is no longer read.
remediation: Rename the env var to `ARGOCD_REPO_SERVER_OTLP_HEADERS` in the patch or Helm values that sets it (or move the value to the `otlp.headers` key of argocd-cmd-params-cm, which the shipped Deployment already maps) before upgrading; otherwise repo-server exports traces without the collector headers (typically its auth token).
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("repo-server$")) | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]?.name] | index("ARGOCD_REPO_OTLP_HEADERS")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # Deployments printed still set the old name

title: Applications with `ServerSideApply=true` switch to Server-Side Diff — validating webhooks now run at diff time

detection.reason: presence-only projection of the Application's sync options, as the agent emits it; an Application that already opts in or out through the `argocd.argoproj.io/compare-options` annotation, or a controller already running with `controller.diff.server.side`, is still named, and a resource-level `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options` annotation is not scanned

quote: Applications that enable the `ServerSideApply=true` sync option now calculate diffs using Server-Side Diff, which performs a Server-Side Apply dry-run against the kube-apiserver.
remediation: No change is required. Expect extra kube-apiserver dry-run load and diff errors (instead of sync errors) from resources a validating webhook rejects; fix those resources, or keep the legacy diff for an Application by annotating it `argocd.argoproj.io/compare-options: ServerSideDiff=false`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applications -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions // [] | index("ServerSideApply=true")) | select((.metadata.annotations["argocd.argoproj.io/compare-options"] // "") | test("ServerSideDiff=(true|false)") | not) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # Applications printed change diff strategy in 3.6

title: RollingSync ApplicationSets wait for every owned Application to refresh before progressing a step

detection.reason: strategyType is projected on every ApplicationSet (`spec.strategy.type`, "" when unset); the strategy only takes effect when the applicationset controller runs with progressive syncs enabled, which is not checked

quote: If you're using ApplicationSets with progressive sync, and are managing many applications, you might see some delays in applications progressing through steps.
remediation: No change is required; expect slower step progression for large RollingSync ApplicationSets because every owned Application is refreshed and reconciled before a step starts. Revisit rollout timeouts or alerts that assume the old pace.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applicationsets -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.strategy.type == "RollingSync") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " steps=" + ((.spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps // []) | length | tostring)'

title: Argo CD traces: parent-based sampling honours inbound "not sampled", and span attribute names change

detection.reason: whether tracing is on (flag, env var or argocd-cmd-params-cm `otlp.address`), whether an upstream proxy propagates `traceparent`, and which dashboards key on span attributes are not projected facts

quote: Because the sampler is parent-based, a request that already carries a W3C `traceparent` marked *not sampled* is no longer recorded, even with `--otlp-sample-ratio=1.0`.
remediation: If Argo CD exports traces: set the same `--otlp-sample-ratio` on every component, expect requests that arrive marked not-sampled to be dropped, and update dashboards/alerts for the semantic-convention v1.42/v1.43 attribute renames (`server.address`/`server.port` now carry the gRPC dial target, not the peer IP).
verifyCommand: kubectl get cm -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("argocd-cmd-params-cm$")) | .metadata.namespace + " otlp.address=" + (.data["otlp.address"] // "(unset)")' # unset everywhere = tracing off, nothing to do
coversNotes: Tracing sampler is now parent-based and configurable

title: GitOps Promoter PromotionStrategy/ChangeTransferPolicy report Healthy (not Progressing) during a promotion

detection.reason: Promoter custom resources and the alerting that reads their health are not collected; the hint names the Promoter CRDs when they are installed

quote: Argo CD's built-in health checks for `promoter.argoproj.io/PromotionStrategy` and `promoter.argoproj.io/ChangeTransferPolicy` now report `Healthy` instead of `Progressing` when a promotion is in progress.
remediation: Change alerting or automation that treats `Progressing` on these resources as "a promotion is running" to read the health message or the Promoter status fields instead; nothing to do without GitOps Promoter.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group == "promoter.argoproj.io") | .metadata.name' # empty = GitOps Promoter not installed, rule does not apply

title: CloudNativePG `Database` is Healthy only once applied — sync waves now wait for it

detection.reason: CloudNativePG Database objects and the sync waves that order around them are not collected; the hint names the CloudNativePG CRDs when they are installed

quote: It reports `Healthy` only once the operator has applied the current generation (`status.applied` with a matching `status.observedGeneration`), so a sync wave acts as a real dependency barrier for it instead of treating the not-yet-applied Database as healthy.
remediation: No change is required; Applications that ship a `postgresql.cnpg.io/Database` before later sync waves now wait until the operator applies it, so a Database the operator never applies leaves the sync Progressing — check its status if a sync stalls after the upgrade.
verifyCommand: kubectl get databases.postgresql.cnpg.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.status.applied != true or .status.observedGeneration != .metadata.generation) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # Databases printed would block their sync wave today
